description.nb:
Key to all species in Norway in the polychaete families Ampharetidae and Melinnidae.
Tom Alvestad, University Museum of Bergen.
License: CC BY 4.0.
In the browser Microsoft Edge parts of the key do not work. Chrome or Firefox is recommended.

title.nb: Anterior acicular neurochaetae absent (notochaetae start before neurochaetae): Family Ampharetidae
Anterior acicular neurochaetae present (neurochaetae start before notochaetae): Family Melinnidae
Postbranchial hooks with gently curved tips
Postbranchial hooks with strongly curved tips
Prostomium with well-defined anterior and posterior parts, separated by a pair of deep transverse nuchal grooves that almost meet mid-dorsally: Family Melinnidae
Prostomium with longtitudinal ridges, but without obvious transverse nuchal grooves
Prostomium with longtitudinal ridges and obvious transverse nuchal grooves
Prostomium trilobed; middle lobe drawn out into horns
Prostomium trilobed; middle lobe not drawn out into horns
Prostomium not divided into lobes; longtitudinal ridges and obvious nuchal grooves absent
Eyespots on prostomium absent (eyespots will fade away in alcohol as most other pigmentation)
Paleae short (same length or shorter than thoracic notochaetae)
Branchiae in two groups of four, arranged in rhomboid pattern
Branchiae in two groups of four, not arranged in rhomboid pattern
Within each branchial group, the two foremost  branchiae in transverse row, the two following branchiae in longitudinal row
Three branchiae in each group in transverse row, the fourth branchia behind inner branchia of anterior row
Three branchiae in each group in transverse row, the fourth branchia more or less behind the middle branchia of anterior row
Three branchiae in each group in transverse row, the fourth branchia a distance behind the outer branchia of anterior row
Three branchiae in each group arranged in triangle, the fouth branchia closer to mid-dorsum and obliquely behind the posterior one of the three

Branchial placement otherwise, with one or several of the following characteristics: anteriormost pair of branchiae partly fused lengthwise; branchiae firmly attached and unlikely to fall off; anteriormost pair of branchiae thicker than other pairs
Small branchial gap (about the same width as one branchial base diameter)
Large branchial gap (about the same width as two or more branchial base diameters)
Lower lip enlarged (as long as or longer than prostomium)
Mouth tentacles of two types: one long and thick tentacle and several small ones
All tentacles smooth and of similar size
All tentacles papillous and of similar size
Number of thoracic chaetigers, excluding paleae
Thoracic chaetigers of equal length or gradually increasing in length posteriorly
Posterior 4 thoracic chaetigers clearly longer than preceeding ones
11th pair of thoracic notopodia slightly elevated and joined by ridge across dorsum
12th pair of thoracic notopodia elevated and laterally enlarged; notochaetae usually crossing mid-dorsally
14th pair of thoracic notopodia achaetous and transformed into dorsolateral fan with pointed lateral wings and a low ridge across dorsum
Neuropodial dorsal cirri on posterior thoracic chaetigers
Neuropodial dorsal cirri on posterior thoracic chaetigers long
Neuropodial dorsal cirri on posterior thoracic chaetigers short or absent
Neuropodia dorsal cirri on abdominal chaetigers
Abdominal neuropodial dorsal cirri short or absent
Pygidium with two lateral rounded lobes
Pygidum with several large and small lobes
Pygidium with a number of small equally sized papillae
